lessons.title: Volume
objectives: Define volume; its SI unit is the m³ (also L, mL, cm³; 1 mL = 1 cm³)
Read a graduated cylinder: eye at the level of the bottom of the meniscus
Find the volume of an irregular solid by displacement: V = V₂ − V₁
Calculate the volume of regular solids (cube, box, cylinder, sphere)

lessons.title: Free surface of liquids
objectives: The free surface of a liquid at rest is plane and horizontal
Draw the free surface in tilted or closed containers
Communicating vessels: a liquid at rest reaches the same level in all branches

lessons.title: Mass and density
objectives: Mass is the quantity of matter (kg); measure it with a balance
Density ρ = m / V (g/cm³ or kg/m³)
Identify a substance from its density; predict floating and sinking

lessons.title: Current and voltage in grouped lamps
objectives: Series: same current; the voltages add up
Parallel: the junction law for currents; the same voltage across each branch
Identical lamps share the voltage or the current equally
Voltage across a switch: 0 when closed, the whole voltage of its path when open

lessons.title: DC voltage: measurement and grouping
objectives: Voltmeter in parallel; V and COM terminals; U_BA = −U_AB; choose the calibre
Oscilloscope: U = S_v × y (number of divisions); sweep on or off
Voltage laws in series and in parallel; switch voltage

lessons.title: Alternating sinusoidal voltage
objectives: DC versus AC voltage; the 4 characteristics of an AC voltage
U_m = S_v × y, T = S_h × x, f = 1/T
Effective value U_eff = U_m / √2; the voltmeter in AC mode reads U_eff

lessons.title: Rectilinear motion
objectives: Position and displacement vectors written with the unit vector i
Average velocity; instantaneous velocity from a dot print: Vₙ = Mₙ₋₁Mₙ₊₁ / 2τ
Acceleration aₙ = (Vₙ₊₁ − Vₙ₋₁) / 2τ; uniform vs uniformly varied motion; a·V sign test
Time equations v = at + V₀ and x = ½at² + V₀t + x₀; position and velocity graphs

lessons.title: Part 1: horizontal and inclined planes
objectives: 1st law (inertia), 2nd law ΣF = m·a, 3rd law (interaction)
Forces: weight, normal reaction, friction, tension; project on x and y
Motion on a horizontal plane and on an inclined plane, with or without friction

lessons.title: Part 2: motion of a projectile
objectives: Only the weight acts, so a = g; uniform on x, uniformly varied on y
Time equations, trajectory (parabola), summit and range
Horizontal launch from a height; velocity at a point

lessons.title: Review: planes and projectiles
objectives: Combine both parts in exam-style problems

lessons.title: Forces and the resultant force
objectives: Name and represent the usual forces: weight, normal reaction, tension, friction, applied force
The 4 characteristics of a force; draw it to scale
Resultant of collinear forces (same or opposite direction) and of perpendicular forces
Orthonormal system: Fx = F cos α, Fy = F sin α; R = √(Rx² + Ry²), tan θ = Ry / Rx
